gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP (2011 int$) 1,004,766,131,386 / population 116,786,962 = 8,603. Range +/-15%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 1,255,173,180,995 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 1,004,766,131,386 2011 int$. Range +/-15% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/PHL/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD?format=json Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 1.30% of GDP in 2025. Factbook: 1.7% (2024 incl. pensions).

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 27.0% of GDP (World Bank).

foodSurplus.note: Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/PHL/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 20.5% (2025). s proxied by the rice self-sufficiency ratio 0.77 (2022, PSA via https://businessmirror.com.ph/2023/10/10/rice-sufficiency-level-falls-to-24-year-low/), rice being the main calorie source. Mid 1 - 0.205/0.77 = 0.73. Low: a x 1.3 (larger rural households), s 0.72 = 0.63. High: s 0.815 (2021) = 0.75. Import dependence: world's largest rice importer; wheat fully imported. Audit follow-up 2026-10-29: 0.0 -> 0.73, rule changed: value is the share of production not eaten by the farm population, import dependence goes in the note.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 58,251,330 x share of males aged 15-19 9.937% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 1,157,699. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. Austal Balamban / HHI Subic. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_active_Philippine_Navy_ships)

railKm.note: asOf 2016: 509 route-km (World Bank). World Bank value from 2016; CIA Factbook 77 km operational (low); North-South Commuter Railway under construction.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 2 large + 4 medium = 6 (Manila, Cebu, Davao, Batangas, Subic...).

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: 5,626 thousand DWT under the national flag. Range +/-10%.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Archipelago, US logistics support assumed (EDCA sites).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Carabao (water buffalo) ~2.8 million (not from FAO data); militarily marginal.

nuclearWarheads.note: FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 lists nine nuclear-armed states; the Philippines is not one of them.

basesAbroad.name: BRP Sierra Madre outpost, Second Thomas (Ayungin) Shoal

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1-1.2: archipelago and mountainous jungle interior.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with a 2026 order of battle. Population inside the ne: border (World Bank 2025). Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Counts from the Wikipedia Philippine Army equipment list, Navy active-ship list and Air Force article. Doctrine archetype-modern-small-state: a light, alliance-dependent territorial-defence force (Comprehensive Archipelagic Defense Concept) despite a large population. CAFGU militia and Coast Guard (paramilitary per IISS 100,650) excluded. A-29 count from memory of the delivery, grade C.
